drafts.summary: Keyboard editing test for TodoMVC failed at initial focus traversal. The test created a task 'Pick up a prescription' and attempted to reach the edit control via Tab navigation, but focus escaped to an anchor element instead of the editor. Subsequent cancellation and save flows were never executed.

body.title: Edit a task using the keyboard; Escape preserves the original task

assertions.label: The task can be edited from the keyboard
Escape and subsequent focus change preserve the prior title
An intentional edit is still saved
Task is created and visible in the list
Focus reaches the task completion toggle via Tab
Pressing Enter on focused task opens the editor
Editor becomes visible after opening
Editor closes when Escape is pressed
Editor closes when Enter saves the edit

obligations.text: Focus must remain within the task title element after tab-edit action so that Enter can open the editor. Observed: focus escaped to an anchor element (trace sequence 21-22).
Task 'Pick up a prescription' was created successfully via Enter key on the new task input.
Tab navigation from new task input reached the task completion toggle (todo-item-toggle).
Escape key during editing must preserve the original task title. This transition was never reached because the editor never opened (keyboard-entry failed).
Intentional edit saved via Enter must update the task title. This transition was never reached because the editor never opened (keyboard-entry failed).
Pressing Enter on focused task title should open the editor. Not observed because focus escaped before this action.
Pressing Escape in the editor should close it without saving. Not observed because editor never opened.
Pressing Enter in the editor should save and close it. Not observed because editor never opened.

ambiguities: Why did focus escape to an anchor element ('a') instead of the editor after tab-edit? The binding for 'editor' uses role='textbox' name='Edit todo' but the trace shows focus on 'a'.
Is the 'taskTitle' binding (data-testid='todo-item-label') the correct element to receive focus for editing, or should focus go directly to the editor?
Does the application require a double-click or specific key (Enter/F2) on the task label to enter edit mode, rather than Tab focus alone?
The 'tab-edit' action presses Tab from the toggle; perhaps an additional Tab is needed to reach the task label, then Enter to edit.
No screen-reader or accessibility tree data captured; cannot verify ARIA roles or focus management expectations.
The test stopped at the first failed assertion; no checkpoint data exists for cancelled-value or saved-value.

drafts.revisionNotes: Automated development review: the toggle assertion uses the task-title binding at the checkbox checkpoint; the close assertions require focus in an editor already required to be hidden. Remove these contradictory model additions. Preserve all three original task obligations plus supported added checks. This is not independent human contract review.
drafts.summary: An explicit reviewer correction removed unsupported proposed assertions. Original protected requirements are unchanged.

repairs.summary: Inspecting the permitted source for the observed transition.
repairs.error: The model source quotation did not match the cited lines. No patch was applied.

repairs.summary: The keyboard navigation fails because the task label (todo-item-label) is not focusable via Tab and doesn't handle Enter key to open the editor. The fix adds tabIndex={0} and an onKeyDown handler to the label element in item.jsx to make it keyboard-accessible, allowing Enter to trigger handleDoubleClick which opens the editor.

locations.reason: The label is the task title element that should receive keyboard focus and open the editor on Enter. It currently only has onDoubleClick, no tabIndex or onKeyDown for Enter, so Tab navigation skips it and focus escapes to footer links.
This callback opens the editor by setting isWritable=true. It should also be callable from a keyboard handler on the label for Enter key.

repairs.summary: The Escape key during task editing does not close the editor because the Input component lacks Escape key handling and the Item component lacks a cancellation path. Two changes are required: (1) Add Escape key handling in Input.jsx that invokes an onCancel prop, and (2) Add an onCancel handler in Item.jsx that sets isWritable to false without dispatching UPDATE_ITEM, then pass it to the Input component.

locations.reason: The handleKeyDown callback only responds to Enter. Escape key presses fall through with no action, leaving the editor open. Adding an Escape branch that invokes a new onCancel prop (or calls onBlur with the original value) will allow the editor to close and preserve the prior title.

The Input receives only onSubmit and onBlur, both wired to commitEdit. A cancellation path is missing; the component must pass an onCancel handler that sets isWritable to false without dispatching UPDATE_ITEM.

The label's keydown handler opens the editor on Enter. This works correctly in the second replay (event 24-26). No change needed here, but the citation confirms the editor-open transition functions when focus reaches the label.
